vat.summary: UK VAT. Standard 20%, reduced 5%, zero 0%. Used-car dealers often use the second-hand margin scheme — do not compute a margin from memory; read the books.

facts.note: Specified goods (domestic fuel, some energy-saving materials, etc.)
Specified goods (most food, books, children's clothes, etc.) — not the same as exempt
Threshold moves. Last widely published step was £90,000 from 1 April 2024. Do not file from this file.

payroll.summary: PAYE is how UK employers run payroll: income tax and National Insurance through HMRC, usually via payroll software (Xero, Sage, etc.).

facts.note: Pay As You Earn. RTI reports to HMRC each pay run.
Payroll follows the UK tax year, not the calendar year.
Rates, codes and YTD sit in the payroll product. Read them from there; do not invent a tax code.

self-assessment.summary: Self Assessment is the UK return for sole traders, some company directors, and people with untaxed income.

facts.note: Tax year 2025/26 is due 31 January 2027. Paper is earlier (31 October).
Balancing payment and first payment on account typically due the same day.

corporation-tax.summary: UK companies pay Corporation Tax on profits. Main rate 25%; small-profits rate 19% with marginal relief between the bands.

facts.note: Profits above the upper limit (historically £250,000). Confirm current limits.
Profits at or below the lower limit (historically £50,000).

income-tax.summary: England, Wales and Northern Ireland share the main Income Tax rates. Scotland sets its own bands. Always ask which nation.

facts.note: Long frozen at £12,570. Do not assume it has moved.
Scottish Income Tax bands are set in Edinburgh. A Scottish taxpayer is not on the rUK table.
